issues.legal_issue: An indeterminate and fluctuating group of village residents cannot acquire a fishery right by lost grant, prescription, or adverse possession merely through use based on residence.
material_facts: The claimed right was asserted by fishermen residing in several villages, whose number and membership changed through births, deaths, and movement between villages.
The evidence showed fishermen using the fishery at different times with the leave and licence of some owners, but did not establish a continuous tenancy or uniform rent paid to all owners.
The fishermen were not shown to form a corporate body or to hold the right as beneficiaries of a trust.
issues.conclusion: The fishermen could not establish a right to the fishery by lost grant, prescription, or adverse possession on the evidence presented.
issues.legal_principle: The doctrine of lost grant is a technical means of establishing title by prescription and requires a grantee capable of receiving a grant. A fluctuating, unascertained group of inhabitants is not such a grantee; residence or a shared interest does not itself make the group a corporate body. Use with permission does not establish the claimed right by adverse possession or prescription. The Court relied on Lakshmidhar Misra v. Rangalal and Asrabulla v. Kiamatulla.

rule.if: fishery_right_claim and fluctuating_resident_group and (no_identifiable_grantee or no_corporate_body_or_trust) and permissive_or_intermittent_use

predicates.fishery_right_claim: A group of people claimed a right to use a fishery.
predicates.fluctuating_resident_group: The people claiming the right were residents of a locality whose membership could change through births, deaths, or movement.
predicates.no_identifiable_grantee: The evidence did not identify a stable person or body capable of receiving a grant of the claimed right.
predicates.no_corporate_body_or_trust: The people claiming the right were not shown to constitute a corporate body or to be beneficiaries of a trust.
predicates.permissive_or_intermittent_use: The evidence showed use by different people at different times with permission, rather than established continuous use under a uniform tenancy.

issues.definition: When a changeable group of residents claims a fishery right without an identifiable grantee or corporate or trust structure, and the evidence shows only permissive or intermittent use, the group cannot acquire the right by lost grant or prescription.

issues.legal_issue: An unchallenged possession order made after notice to the interested owners can become final and extinguish their right to recover possession of the fishery.
material_facts: A criminal proceeding concerned possession of the fishery, and the magistrate found the fishermen before him to be in possession.
The magistrate ordered that their possession continue until eviction in due course of law and prohibited disturbance in the meantime.
All the owners had notice of the proceeding, but they did not take steps to challenge the order within the applicable limitation period.
issues.conclusion: The order became final against the owners, and their right to recover possession of the fishery was extinguished.
issues.legal_principle: Section 145 of the Criminal Procedure Code applies to disputes concerning possession of water and, under subsection (2), includes fisheries. Article 47 of the Limitation Act required a challenge within the prescribed period. Because the owners had notice and did not challenge the possession order within that period, it became final and their right to recover possession was extinguished.

rule.if: fishery_possession_proceeding and possession_order_for_claimants and owners_received_notice and owners_failed_to_challenge_within_limitation_period

predicates.fishery_possession_proceeding: A proceeding concerned competing claims to possession of a fishery.
predicates.possession_order_for_claimants: The decision-maker found the claimants in possession and directed that their possession continue unless they were evicted lawfully.
predicates.owners_received_notice: The owners whose possession claim was affected received notice of the proceeding.
predicates.owners_failed_to_challenge_within_limita: The owners did not bring a challenge within the applicable limitation period.

issues.definition: If a fishery possession proceeding results in an order preserving the claimants' possession, the owners receive notice, and they do not challenge the order within the applicable period, their right to recover possession is extinguished.

issues.legal_issue: A possession order benefits only the persons who were parties to the proceeding and their successors in interest unless other persons are shown to have been represented.
material_facts: Twelve fishermen were named as the second party in the possession proceeding.
The record did not establish who else, if anyone, was represented by those fishermen.
Some fishermen claiming rights in the later suit were neither parties nor shown to be successors in interest of parties to the earlier proceeding.
issues.conclusion: Only the fishermen who were parties to the possession proceeding, or their successors in interest, could rely on its order; the other claimants could not derive a right from it.
issues.legal_principle: The benefit of a possession order extends to the parties in whose favour it was made and their successors in interest. Without evidence that other persons were represented in the proceeding, they cannot claim the benefit of the order.

rule.if: fishery_possession_proceeding and claimant_not_named_in_proceeding and no_evidence_of_representation and no_successor_relationship

predicates.fishery_possession_proceeding: A proceeding determined possession of a fishery between identified parties.
predicates.claimant_not_named_in_proceeding: A person later claiming the benefit of the order was not named as a party in the possession proceeding.
predicates.no_evidence_of_representation: The evidence did not show that a party to the proceeding represented that person.
predicates.no_successor_relationship: The person was not shown to be a successor in interest of a party to the proceeding.

issues.definition: A person who was neither a party to a fishery possession proceeding nor represented by or succeeding to a party cannot rely on the proceeding's possession order.

issues.legal_issue: An exclusive fishing right may be confined to a particular class of fish or season without being defeated by another person's right to fish at another time or for another class of fish.
material_facts: The possession order supported a right to fish exclusively for a particular class of fish during a specified season.
The competing owner's claimed fishing rights concerned other fish or other periods.
The dispute concerned whether such limited rights could be exclusive.
issues.conclusion: A right to fish exclusively in a fishery for a particular class of fish during a particular season is not defeated merely because another person has a right to fish for other fish or at another time.
issues.legal_principle: An exclusive right of fishing at a given place means that no other person has a co-extensive right with the holder. The existence of a right to fish for another class of fish or during another season does not negate that exclusivity. The Court referred to section 145 of the Criminal Procedure Code and Halsbury's Laws of England, Hailsham Edition, volume 15, paragraph 59.

predicates.fishery_right_dispute: A dispute concerned competing rights to fish in the same fishery.
predicates.right_limited_by_fish_class_or_season: The claimed right applied only to a particular class of fish, a particular season, or both.
predicates.other_persons_right_is_not_coextensive: Any other person's fishing right applied to a different class of fish or a different period.

issues.definition: A fishing right confined to a fish class or season can be exclusive when another person's right does not cover the same fish and period.

issues.legal_issue: A change in a river's course does not by itself defeat a possession-based fishing right when the old and new channels remain parts of the same connected fishery.
material_facts: The river had changed course after the possession proceeding.
The old and new channels comprised one connected sheet of water forming the same fishery.
The claimants' fishing activity concerned that connected fishery.
issues.conclusion: The change in the river's course did not affect the claimants' possession of the fishery or the effect of the earlier possession order.
issues.legal_principle: Where the old and new channels form one connected sheet of water within the same fishery, a change in the river's course does not interrupt or alter the relevant possession. The Court observed that fish follow the river and fishermen follow the fish.

predicates.fishery_possession_dispute: A dispute concerned possession of a fishery associated with a river.
predicates.river_course_changed: The river changed its course after the relevant possession was established.
predicates.old_and_new_channels_form_connected_fish: The old and new river channels remained parts of one connected sheet of water comprising the same fishery.

issues.definition: When a river changes course but its old and new channels remain one connected fishery, the change does not defeat the possession right.
